sections.overview: Pseudocyttus maculatus, the smooth oreo, is a deepwater fish in the family Oreosomatidae.
sections.identification: Adults are bluish grey to grey-brown; juveniles have dark blue blotches. The black oreo Allocyttus niger is a related fishery species.
sections.habitat: It lives close to the seabed along deep continental slopes, commonly at depths of roughly six hundred to fifteen hundred metres in New Zealand waters.
sections.diet: A study of the Chatham Rise found that smooth oreos fed mainly on salps and amphipods; diet composition varied with fish size.
sections.behavior: The species is commercially fished in New Zealand and may be taken in targeted oreo fisheries or as bycatch in orange roughy fisheries.
sections.reproduction: New Zealand fisheries summaries estimate that females mature at about thirty-one years and spawn from October to December; these figures concern the monitored fishery stock.
sections.ecology: Unlike black oreo, which ate amphipods, salps and small decapods in the same study, smooth oreo fed mostly on salps and amphipods.
sections.conservation: Oreo catches in New Zealand are managed under a quota system; this management covers several related species together.
